title: Competing Three-Dimensional Mechanisms in Compressor Flows
rights: All rights reserved. The paper is linked from its authoritative repository record and is not redistributed with this dataset.
summary: Explains how the transverse pressure gradient produced by three-dimensional compressor-blade stacking governs separation mode, loss generation and design uncertainty.
summaryBrief: Relates compound lean to competing corner- and trailing-edge-separation mechanisms, aerodynamic loss and compressor design risk.
summaryExtended: The paper treats the transverse pressure gradient as a central control on three-dimensional compressor stator behaviour. Increasing three-dimensional stacking strengthens this gradient and can move the limiting flow mechanism from abrupt open corner separation toward more progressive trailing-edge separation. The same change can increase design-point loss through additional downstream wake mixing. Maps of lean and pitch-to-chord ratio expose a trade-off between minimum loss, operating range and confidence in CFD predictions, making the paper directly relevant to interpreting the compound-lean trends in this sample dataset.

keyFindings.title: Transverse pressure gradient governs separation topology
keyFindings.detail: Changing three-dimensional stacking changes the blade-surface transverse pressure gradient and therefore the dominant separation mechanism.

keyFindings.title: Stronger stacking changes the failure mode
keyFindings.detail: Increasing the transverse pressure gradient can replace sudden open corner separation with progressive three-dimensional trailing-edge separation.

keyFindings.title: Design-point loss and range have different optima
keyFindings.detail: The lowest design-point loss and the widest incidence range do not occur at the same amount of lean, creating a practical design trade-off.

keyFindings.title: Wake mixing explains the loss increase
keyFindings.detail: The increase in total loss associated with a stronger transverse pressure gradient is attributed primarily to increased downstream wake mixing.

keyFindings.title: Low-stacking designs carry greater prediction risk
keyFindings.detail: Open corner separations are sensitive to inlet-condition errors, so reduced stacking can make the predicted operating range substantially more uncertain.

citations: Taylor, J. V. and Miller, R. J. Competing Three-Dimensional Mechanisms in Compressor Flows. Journal of Turbomachinery 139(2), 021009. https://doi.org/10.1115/1.4034685
